entries.title: Daniel 8:1
segments: At the first; in the first year of Belshazzar's reign,

. 
 
vv 1-8, 20-22. 
 
When God has purposes to be accomplished by a nation, he arms it with invincible strength; when the work assigned is done, he takes away its strength and gives it up to the power of others; and these, in like manner, execute his high counsels, while they may be intent only upon carrying out their own schemes of ambition and conquest.

entries.title: Daniel 8:2
segments:
Shushan; Susa, the winter residence of the Persian kings.  It lay on the river Ulai, now called Kerah, which enters the united stream of the Euphrates and Tigris from the north-east. 
 
  Elam; between Babylonia and Persia proper, having Media on the north, and the Persian gulf on the south.

entries.title: Daniel 8:3
segments:
A ram; the united kingdoms of Media and Persia, which are represented by the two horns. 
 
  One was higher than the other, and the higher came up last; Persia, though the younger, became under Cyrus the ruling power.

entries.title: Daniel 8:4
segments: Westward, and northward, and southward; the directions in which the Persian empire extended its conquests.

entries.title: Daniel 8:5
segments:
A he-goat; the Grecian empire. 
 
  Touched not the ground; these words denote the incredible swiftness of Alexander's conquests, who is the "notable horn between his eyes."

entries.title: Daniel 8:7
segments: Stamped upon him; Alexander utterly demolished the Persian monarchy.

entries.title: Daniel 8:8
segments:
Was broken; Alexander died at Babylon in the zenith of his power. 
 
  Came up four; upon his death his kingdom was divided into four.

entries.title: Daniel 8:9
segments:
Out of one of them; out of Syria, which was one of the four kingdoms. 
 
  A little horn; it is generally agreed that this represents the power of Antiochus Epiphanes.  About the 171 before Christ he commenced a bloody persecution against the Jews, in the progress of which he plundered Jerusalem, slaughtered an immense number of its inhabitants, profaned the temple and altar with swine's flesh, and finally took away the daily sacrifice, substituting the four monarchies, which sprung out of the ruins of Alexander's empire. 
 
  The east; Persia. 
 
  The pleasant land; Palestine.

vv 9-14, 23-25. 
 
The wisdom of God has often permitted his church to be wasted by fierce and bloody persecutors, who had all the advantages for destroying her that power and policy could command; yet the result has been, that his people have been purified and made more prosperous by their sufferings, whole their persecutors have miserably perished.

entries.title: Daniel 8:10
segments: The host of heaven--the stars; probably a figurative description of the Jewish princes and spiritual rulers.

entries.title: Daniel 8:11
segments: The prince of the host; this seems to mean God himself, who had established the Jewish state.

entries.title: Daniel 8:12
segments: A host was given--the daily sacrifice; that is, according to our version, power was given him to take away the daily sacrifice,

; but many prefer to render, " A host was given up to him, along with the daily sacrifice;" that is, the Jewish host mentioned in the preceding verses. 
 
  By reason of transgression; literally, "by transgression;" either by reason of the transgression of God's people, or in the little horn's transgression against God.

entries.title: Daniel 8:13
segments: The transgression of desolation; or, "the desolating transgression;" that is, the heathen in God's sanctuary, polluting and desolating it.  Compare

entries.title: Daniel 8:14
segments: Two thousand and three hundred days; literally, "two thousand and three hundred evenings and mornings,"

.  This peculiar form of expression seems to have been chosen here to represent so many literal days, which include the whole period of Antiochus' persecutions.  The time when the daily sacrifice was suspended was, according to Josephus, three years. 
 
  Cleansed; by a new dedication to God.  This was by Judas Maccabaeus, before Christ 165.

entries.title: Daniel 8:16
segments: Between the banks of Ulai; the voice called from the river itself.

entries.title: Daniel 8:17
segments: At the time of the end; the same as, "the last end of the indignation,"
, and "the latter time of their kingdom,"
.  The vision refers to a great crisis in the history of the Jews, and which is in itself a type of a still mightier crisis in the distant future.  See notes on

entries.title: Daniel 8:18
segments: I was in a deep sleep; or, "I fell into a deep sleep," overpowered by the brightness of the vision.

entries.title: Daniel 8:23
segments:
Transgressors; this seems to mean the transgressors among God's people. 
 
  Dark sentences; wily plots and stratagems.

entries.title: Daniel 8:24
segments: Not by his own power; either, not by his proper might, but by craft and policy; or, by a power given him from on high.

entries.title: Daniel 8:25
segments:
By peace; by attacking them unawares under pretences of friendship. 
 
  Without hand; without human hand.  He perished by a violent and distressing sickness inflicted by God's hand.

entries.title: Daniel 8:26
segments:
vv 26-27. 
 
  Vision of the evening and the morning; see note

. 
 
  Shut thou up the vision--none understood it; he was not then to make known the interpretation of the vision, which still presents many difficulties to the ablest commentators.

entries.title: Daniel 8:27
segments: A glimpse of the sufferings that were coming upon his people overcame the prophet's strength, and unfitted him for business.  How merciful, then, is that arrangement which hides from God's children the future troubles that are appointed for them and the church.  Yet when the hour for undergoing them arrives, they receive strength both to bear them and to triumph over them.
